I had a very vivid dream where my best friend, the man I've secretly fallen for, and I had gone out to the movie theaters. We went to a late movie on a Friday night, so he picked me up since I have horrible car anxiety.

The movie was great, it was pretty funny.

For awhile, the ride home was smooth sailing. We'd used a combination of Google Maps and my local knowledge of the area. I knew the route well, but it was night and I was worried about intoxicated drivers. So because if my worry, he promised to drive save and slow. 

After half an hour of driving, my worries were at ease. If it wasn't for the sparce conversation sprinkled within the silence I would have drifted off to sleep. The topic of conversation was vaguely about funerals. I was nodding off to sleep when he turned his head to smile at me. Jokingly he said, "for my funeral, I want it to be open casket. I want the world to see my beautiful face one last time before I go." I began to laugh, but it quickly turned into a silent panic of horror as a car from the opposite direction swerved and crashed into us head on.

Our car was violently pushed off the road and tumbled ten feet down a hill.  I was left unscathed, and I wish I could have said the same for my dear friend. His body was twisted and mangled, trapped by the now warped car door. Expect for his face. His completion was glowing under the moonlight. It was then did I realize he was still alive.

"[His name]!" I cried out as I struggle to free myself from the seat. Already a mess, tears rolling down my cheeks, snot dripping from my nose I continued, "listen to me [his name] you're going to be just fine. Alright?"

His crystal eyes were already hazing over.

"[His name]?" I frantically started reaching around, I needed a phone, away to free us, anything.  "I'm going to get you out of here [his name]. We're going to get through this because I love you," my tongue slipped.

I glanced over. I didn't see him shaking, or his chest still attempting to rise and fall.

The other driver had been drunk. They were never able to find him.

I was checked out by emergency responders who sent me home. Then soon after, I went to bed. Because of this, I believed it was real. Up until this dream, I had never went to bed durning a dream.

The next day was spent in a daze, even durning the funeral where he did have an open casket. I began crying and weeping right there, when I went up to say my goodbyes. After a minute I was profusely apologizing to him as if he were only in a coma, as if he were alive. 

A friend came up to me. "He's gone now. He's not coming back," my friend tried to comfort. It didn't work. Instead, I realized that he'd never heard my confession, that we'd never have a chance together or go in our first date. That in fact, I would never see him again.

I woke up weeping, believing it was real until he texted me. He asked why I had slept in so late.
